answer: Each identity enters through a single inlet, locks a 60-credit bond, and must present a fresh nectar receipt from verified work each epoch. An oasis registry publishes each receipt, checks it against the identity key and work record, and burns duplicates; a failed check burns the bond. The k-th fake still needs its own bond and fresh receipt, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 credits and need 1,000 verified jobs. A rented-receipt ring fails because a receipt carries its owner's key, so a second use is rejected and both bonds burn. An honest agent pays one bond and earns one receipt from its own work.
